tasks.prompt: Find me remote backend engineering jobs in Bengaluru that pay at least ₹30 lakh a year.
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks that every row satisfies the filters. The Space enforces a filter it is sent (strict=1), so rows satisfy the filters exactly when they reach their own fields: remote, india_place, and ₹30 lakh as salary_min 3000000 with salary_currency INR (without the currency it is priced in USD).

tasks.prompt: What new ML engineer jobs have shown up in the last 24 hours?
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks every row's first_seen is inside the window. "New ... in the last 24 hours" is New to HeadStart, the first_seen filter, which the Space applies to every row; posted_within_days is the employer's date and would not bound first_seen. The role must reach query or keyword as ML or machine learning.

tasks.prompt: Is Stripe hiring more or less than it was two weeks ago?
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks the sign of hiring, which ADR-0272 makes postings opened less closed. The verifier reads /trends for Stripe over 14 days itself and compares the sign of reading.total.move.turnover.net (the netted hiring where the reading has no net) with the direction the answer states; a net within 5% of everything opened and closed may also be called flat. Round-2 critique P1-4 (ADR-0325): where opened and closed cover only part of the window, the answer must say so, naming the day counting began or the days counted.

tasks.prompt: Which companies opened more tech jobs than they closed this week?
tasks.why: Plan §9, ADR-0321: the top five equal /hot's, hidden Operators out, on hiring_now's default Lens, postings opened less closed; Expansion's leader on 2026-09-29, Bosch Group, was re-counting its own flag disowned. The verifier reads /hot itself, drops the hidden_by_default Operators, and needs at least four of the top five named. Round-2 critique P1-3 (ADR-0325): the first company the answer names among the hiring_now rows must not be one the tool flagged as re-counting.

tasks.prompt: Compare Google's and Microsoft's tech hiring over this month.
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks breakdown: company. One read_trends call must name both companies, split by company (the default with two or more, so an absent breakdown passes), over about a month: 30 days, or the days since the month began.

tasks.prompt: How are AI and machine learning roles trending across the whole job index?
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks category. The whole index read in the ai-ml-data-science category, with no company scope.

tasks.prompt: Find entry-level frontend jobs at Citi, and then tell me how Citi's hiring is trending.
tasks.why: Plan §9: the search and the trend must not read two different Citis unsaid. Two paths are right (ADR-0334). Path 1, the substring search: search_jobs' scope line 'company name contains' and read_trends' 'Companies: ' line (one directory company), and the answer says the one is a substring match ('contains'/'substring') and the other one company ('directory'/'largest company'/'one company'). Path 2, find_company then its key: search_jobs' scope line names one directory company ('Scope: company "'), the same kind of read the trend makes, so there is no difference to explain.

tasks.prompt: Find remote contract roles with "Rust" in the job title.
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks keyword. "Rust in the title" is keyword Rust in the title (the default scope), with remote and employment_type contract as filters. Rust may also appear in query, which describes the role. Round-2 critique P1-8 (ADR-0325): the arguments alone passed while 15 of 24 rows were 'Trust' and 'Thrusters', so every row the call returned is read back from /job and must have Rust where a word starts in its title, the keyword's own rule (ADR-0299).

tasks.prompt: Which seniority levels grew in data engineering over the last month?
tasks.why: Plan §9 checks breakdown: level. One read_trends call in data-engineering split by level (the default with a category, so an absent breakdown passes).

tasks.prompt: What are the highest-paying staff engineer roles anywhere, in USD?
tasks.why: Plan §9's two branches, each judged by what it obliges the answer to say (ADR-0334). Path 1, the global browse: a search_jobs call with no query, a staff keyword and a salary sort, which answers 'anywhere' by construction. Path 2, a staff query with a salary sort: the tool orders only the 2,000 closest matches and says so, so the answer must pass that on ('closest', '2,000').

tasks.prompt: 3+ years senior backend in Pune
tasks.why: Plan §9: years and place must land in filters, not in query. Years as max_years of at least 3; Pune as india_place or as location, either being a filter; neither in query.

tasks.prompt: Find Haskell jobs in Indore paying ₹1 crore.
tasks.why: Plan §9: must name the Blocking filter, not say nothing exists. Which filter blocks is data-dependent (/facets drops each filter in turn and names the one recovering the most rows), so argument null accepts whichever one the search_jobs result named; the final answer must mention it by name or as that filter ('salary filter', 'minimum salary', not a bare 'salary', which a ₹1 crore answer says anyway), or by the value the call sent for it (value_names_it, ADR-0334). The live runs of 2026-09-29 named india_place, and every answer said there are no Haskell jobs in Indore at any pay, which names the place: the verifier had failed them for not writing 'india_place'. The cost: an answer that names Indore only in restating the question also passes. If no single filter blocks, no result names one and the task fails; revise it then.

tasks.prompt: Find software engineering jobs in Germany that mention visa sponsorship.
tasks.why: Judged on truth, not on one path (round-3 review SP7, ADR-0333). Path 1, the work_authorization offers_sponsorship filter or checked jobs: the answer names at least one job, and none of them fails sponsorship_polarity's reading of whether it offers sponsorship (a person's label, else a negation check of the eval's own). Path 2, the description keyword (ADR-0274): its answer must say the keyword could only match jobs with a stored description (the search carries 'Descriptions are stored for N of M'), must say that a description mentioning sponsorship may refuse it rather than offer it, and any job it names that does not offer sponsorship must be named on a line saying so. An answer that reports keyword matches as jobs offering sponsorship fails both paths.

tasks.prompt: Which of Stripe's openings are in the AI, ML & Data Science category?
tasks.why: ADR-0274: the category the site and the answers print as a label reaches search_jobs as its id or as that label, which the server reads as the id; either names the same category.

tasks.prompt: Is tech hiring across the whole index rising or falling over the last month?
tasks.why: ADR-0272: on 2026-09-29 the whole index's openings listed rose +111,851 over 30 days while postings opened and closed netted -514, and nothing in that rise was sized, so it was re-counting, not hiring. The answer must take its direction from postings opened and closed, which the verifier reads from /trends itself; a net within 5% of everything opened and closed may also be called flat. It must also say that opened and closed cover only part of the 30 days, as t03's must (ADR-0325).

tasks.prompt: Find data engineering jobs in Germany that allow remote work.
tasks.why: Round-1 critique P1-3 (ADR-0273): a country outside India is the country filter, not a location substring or a word in query. Germany is country DE, which also takes rows written only 'Berlin' or 'München'; remote is its own filter.

tasks.prompt: Pick one remote backend engineering job and tell me what its posting says about visa sponsorship.
tasks.why: Critique P0-3 (ADR-0277): what a posting says about sponsorship is in its description, which only get_job serves; a search row carries none. Every job id names its ATS and Board before a colon, so any get_job call reading an id from a search passes. Which job is picked is the agent's choice, so the answer itself is not checked.

tasks.prompt: Find me a machine learning engineer job, then show me five more jobs like that one.
tasks.why: Critique P0-3 (ADR-0277): 'jobs like that one' ranks by the posting's own stored vector, which similar_to sends as like=; describing the job again in query would rank by the words instead. search_jobs refuses query beside similar_to, so a successful call with similar_to was ranked by the job alone.

tasks.prompt: Is Strpie hiring engineers right now? Not sure I spelled it right.
tasks.why: ADR-0275, critique rc03: a misspelt company must be found, not answered with 0 jobs. find_company, or search_jobs' nothing-matched answer, offers Stripe with its key; the answer must name Stripe, and some tool result must carry its key greenhouse:stripe.

tasks.prompt: I'm a recruiter. Where is Amazon hiring tech people, and how many of its openings are remote?
tasks.why: ADR-0275, critique P1-5: where a company is hiring and its remote share is company_profile, the only tool that reads locations. One call must name Amazon, by name or by its key amazon:www.amazon.jobs.

tasks.prompt: Give me Stripe's hiring profile: its openings, which job categories they are in, and the seniority mix.
tasks.why: ADR-0275: a company's category mix and seniority mix together are one company_profile call; read_trends answers one of them per call. One call must name Stripe, by name or by its key greenhouse:stripe.

tasks.prompt: A friend sent me the job id greenhouse:nonexistentco:12345. Is it still open?
tasks.why: Round-2 critique (js10b, ADR-0323): an id whose Board serves no job was never a HeadStart id, not a posting that 'most likely closed'. get_job says so when the Board it names serves nothing, and the answer must not report it as closed but as not an id.

tasks.prompt: Which countries is Stripe hiring tech people in, and where most?

tool_results_all: by country as search_jobs' `country` reads each place

tasks.why: Round-2 critique rc02b (ADR-0323): company_profile rolls a company's places up by country, so "Dublin" and "Dublin, Ireland" count as one Ireland. On 2026-09-29 Stripe's served jobs were in the United States (98), Canada (26) and Ireland (23) first; the answer must name the United States and Ireland from that roll-up.

tasks.prompt: I'm thinking of switching into data engineering. What skills do data engineer postings usually ask for, and how many years of experience?
tasks.why: Critique round 2 P1-10 (ADR-0324): what a role's postings ask for is one role_requirements call, counted over a sample, not five get_job reads. The role goes in query, or the category in category.

tasks.prompt: Which skills are most in demand for machine learning engineers in Germany?
tasks.why: ADR-0324: skills in demand are role_requirements' counts, and the place is its country filter (ADR-0273), never words in query.

tasks.prompt: What do cybersecurity job postings typically require? Say how many postings your answer is based on.
tasks.why: ADR-0324: the answer must state its sample honestly. role_requirements says in its first line how many distinct postings it counted over, one per requisition since ADR-0332 (271 of 300 read on 2026-09-29), and how many of them had a description; the final answer must carry one of those numbers as the tool gave it today (ADR-0334), not a number frozen into this task.

tasks.prompt: Find jobs in the Netherlands whose descriptions mention relocation, and show me the second page of results too.
tasks.why: Round-2 critique P0-2 (ADR-0320): two country-scoped "relocation" searches in descriptions both hit the 45 s deadline. The rows a description keyword keeps are now found once and kept, so the second page must come back as a successful call, not a deadline sentence.

tasks.prompt: Did tech hiring rise or fall between 1 and 7 September 2026?

tool_results_all: cannot say whether hiring rose or fell

tasks.why: ADR-0321, critique round 2 P1-2: HeadStart counts postings opened and closed only from 2026-09-25 18:16, so a window before it has no hiring figure, only openings listed, which mix hiring with re-counting. The trend answer must lead with that, and the final answer must pass it on rather than call the change in openings a rise. Round 3's r2 wrote 'HeadStart can't answer this', which says it; the word list now takes 'answer' and 'determine' beside 'say' and 'tell' (ADR-0334).

tasks.prompt: Show me jobs in the AI, ML & Data Science category in Germany.
tasks.why: Round-2 critique P1-5 (ADR-0322): a category across the whole index is its own argument, needing no company and no words in query. category names the family (its id, or its label, which the server reads as the id) and country the place.

tasks.prompt: Find senior backend engineering roles that ask for at least 8 years of experience.
tasks.why: Round-2 critique P1-9 (ADR-0322): a floor on a job's required experience is required_years_at_least, never max_years, which is the user's own experience; the years stay out of query.

tasks.prompt: Find me a backend engineer job at Stripe, then five jobs like it at other companies.
tasks.why: Round-2 critique P2, the risk ADR-0277 names (ADR-0322): jobs like one posting are often that employer's own; similar_to ranks by the posting and exclude_company leaves its employer out.

tasks.prompt: Find IT Associate Software Engineer jobs in the United States. Does any one job appear twice?
tasks.why: Round-2 critique st05b (ADR-0323): one Eversource requisition is served from its Radancy front ('EVERSOURCE') and its Workday Board ('Eversource Energy'). search_jobs lists the second under the first as 'also #N' and says why. Data-dependent: the pair was posted 2026-09-28; retire the task when it closes.

tasks.prompt: Which company is behind the job board oracle:hcbt.fa.em2.oraclecloud.com, and what tech roles does it have open?
tasks.why: Round-2 critique js08b (ADR-0323): that Oracle pod names no company on its own. The answer must name the company the tools name for the Board, as search_jobs' scope line, find_company or company_profile gives it (answer_carries, ADR-0334): the directory's name, once marked '(directory name)', which the Board now serves as its own ('Kotak', 2026-09-29), so the task no longer fixes which. Not the pod's host.

tasks.prompt: How senior are Stripe's open tech roles? Give the split by level.
tasks.why: Round-2 critique P1-9 (ADR-0323): company_profile counts each job once in the Trends level bands, not the Search rail's ceilings where a job stating no experience counts at every level. The answer must give the senior and entry-level bands from that line.

tasks.prompt: Show me as much as you can of the full descriptions of these two postings: ashby:caremessage:c6ef6788-c2d3-4668-8361-8ffd9ce92c1b and clearcompany:firefly:3816581.
tasks.why: Round-2 critique inj03 (ADR-0323): two ids share get_job's 18,000-character budget, so the 9,699-character CareMessage description is cut at its 9,000 share, and the answer says to read that id alone, not to raise max_chars_per_job past what the share allows. Data-dependent: both were open on 2026-09-29.

tasks.prompt: I'm an international student finishing a computer science degree and will need a work visa. Find me three software engineering jobs in the United States that offer visa sponsorship.
tasks.why: Round-3 critique P0-1 (ADR-0333): a keyword search for 'sponsorship' in descriptions led with jobs refusing it (36 of 40 sampled did), and t13 passed while checking only that a description search ran. The verifier judges the answer's truth, not its arguments, and apart from the Space's own rules, so it can see their errors (round-3 review SP8): every row the search_jobs and get_job calls listed is read back from /job, and no job the answer names may be one that does not offer sponsorship. A job in the 660 descriptions a person labelled for ADR-0333 (tests/fixtures/work_authorization_labelled.jsonl) is judged by its label, offers or mixed passing; any other by a plain negation check ('no', 'not', 'without', 'refuse', 'citizenship required') within five words of a sponsorship word in the sentences /job quotes. It catches a labelled job labelled refuses or none, and an unlabelled one whose quoted sponsorship sentence negates. It cannot catch an unlabelled job whose refusal no quoted sentence states, and it fails a right answer whose job offers sponsorship in a sentence that also negates ('no matter your visa status, we sponsor'). The work_authorization offers_sponsorship filter is the way to pass; a keyword answer passes only if every job it names offers it.
